Caribbean

Two Countries
Wearing One Flag.

The country splits in two, and only one half shows up in the search results. Punta Cana's all-inclusive corridor does a beach week with children better than almost anywhere, and it is not the Dominican Republic. Casa de Campo's golf, the Samaná peninsula in whale season and Santo Domingo's colonial core are the other half, and they run on the same December-to-April window.

The Country

Punta Cana Is Not
the Dominican Republic.

The dry season runs December through April, and that is the window. Humpback whales are in Samaná Bay from roughly mid-January to late March. Atlantic hurricane season runs June 1 to November 30. Most trips run six to eight nights. The country splits in two: the all-inclusive corridor around Punta Cana, and Casa de Campo, Samaná and Santo Domingo, which is where the rest of it is.

Two Dominican Republics share one flag. The first is the eastern corridor: a wall of large all-inclusive resorts along the Bávaro and Punta Cana beaches, sold by the room-night, arrived at by charter, left by shuttle. The second is the rest of the island — Casa de Campo above the Chavón gorge, the Samaná peninsula, the colonial core of Santo Domingo, the kiteboarding water at Cabarete, and a mountain range in the middle with towns cold enough at night to need a sweater. The first is what the search results return. The second is what people describe a year later.

That is not an argument against Punta Cana. It does one trip better than almost anywhere in the Caribbean: a beach week with young children, food and drink handled, a short transfer from a big airport, and a pool nobody has to leave. If that is the trip you want, book it and enjoy it. What Punta Cana is not is a way to see the country. There is no town to walk into at the end of the afternoon, and the resort wall is the point rather than a failure of the design.

The decisions that matter here are the ones nobody argues about on a booking site. Which of the four usable airports you land at, and how much daylight the transfer takes off the first day. Whether the calendar is built around whales, golf or neither. Whether the property is chosen by star rating or by the section of beach it sits on. Half the badly planned trips here go wrong in the transfers rather than the hotels.

Where We Send Clients

Six Places Worth Planning Properly

These six are not interchangeable and they do not sit close together. Choosing between them is the first decision on the trip, and it sets the airport and the pace.

La Romana
Casa de Campo
An estate rather than a hotel: villas, a marina, a private beach at Minitas and the best golf in the Caribbean. Altos de Chavón, the stone village above the gorge, sits inside the gate. La Romana's airport is minutes from the entrance, which changes how the first and last days feel.
Teeth of the Dog Villas Altos de Chavón
Explore →
Samaná Peninsula
Las Terrenas & Playa Bonita
A fishing town French and Italian families settled into over four decades, which is why the bakeries and beach kitchens are better than the size of the place suggests. Playa Cosón runs for miles with almost nothing on it. Small owner-run hotels rather than towers, and a walkable town at the end of the day.
Playa Cosón Small Hotels Food Town
Explore →
Samaná
Samaná Bay & Los Haitises
North Atlantic humpbacks winter here to breed and calve, and the bay is the most reliable place in the Caribbean to watch them from a permitted boat. Across the water, Los Haitises National Park is limestone hills standing in mangrove with Taíno cave art inside them. Both sit under national protection rules.
Humpbacks Jan – Mar Los Haitises
Explore →
Distrito Nacional
Santo Domingo
The oldest European city in the Americas, founded in 1498, with the first cathedral and the first university on this side of the Atlantic still standing in the same few streets. UNESCO inscribed the Colonial City in 1990. Two nights here turns a beach trip into a country.
Ciudad Colonial UNESCO 1990 Winter Baseball
Explore →
La Altagracia
Punta Cana & Cap Cana
The corridor that carries most of the country's arrivals, and the right answer for a beach week where nothing needs deciding. Cap Cana is the quieter gated southern end, with a marina and Punta Espada's golf. Choose by the stretch of beach and the neighbours, not the star rating.
All-Inclusive Cap Cana Family Beach
Explore →
Puerto Plata
Cabarete & the North Coast
The thermal wind fills in most afternoons and empties the beach into the water, which is how a village became a kiteboarding town. Puerto Plata has the Victorian old town and the cable car up Mount Isabel de Torres; Damajagua's canyon and Playa Grande's clifftop golf sit close by.

Featured Itineraries

Trips We Plan Often

Four shapes cover almost every Dominican Republic trip worth taking. What separates them is the airport, the calendar and how much of the country you intend to see.

December – April · 6–8 Days
Casa de Campo, With the Golf Sequenced
Fly into La Romana if the schedule allows it: the gate is minutes away, and the trip starts with an afternoon rather than a van. A villa with staff rather than a hotel room, which is the format the estate was built around. Teeth of the Dog early, on a morning when the trade wind is still soft; Dye Fore on a separate day for the gorge holes, with a rest day between them. An evening at Altos de Chavón, and a private boat out of the marina to Catalina or Saona instead of the packaged version that reaches the same beach with three hundred people. Two nights in Santo Domingo at either end turns a golf week into a trip.
Dominican Republic6–8 Days
Plan This Trip
Mid-January – Late March · 7–9 Days
Samaná in Whale Season
The one week of the Dominican calendar that cannot be moved. Base at Las Terrenas or Playa Bonita, in a small owner-run hotel where the beach is a walk rather than a shuttle. Two mornings on the bay with a permitted operator, booked as separate days, because weather takes days off and one booking is one roll of the dice. A day across the water into Los Haitises for the mangrove channels and the cave paintings, which beats any of the sandbar trips. El Limón by horse or on foot depending on the ground. Afternoons in town, where the four o'clock bakery queue tells you who settled here.
Dominican Republic7–9 Days

December – April · 9–11 Days
The City and the Peninsula
Three nights in the Ciudad Colonial to start, in a restored sixteenth-century house rather than a business hotel on the Malecón. Calle Las Damas at opening, the Alcázar de Colón and the cathedral, inside the quarter UNESCO inscribed in 1990 as the first European city in the Americas. If the dates land between October and January, a LIDOM winter-league baseball night is the most Dominican evening available and almost no visitor plans it; confirm the schedule first. Then north-east to Las Terrenas for five or six nights, with the bay, Los Haitises and enough unscheduled afternoons that the second half is a rest rather than a second itinerary.

December – April · 5–7 Days
Punta Cana, Chosen Deliberately
The version of the corridor worth booking, for the family that wants a beach week and no decisions. The property is chosen by the stretch of beach it occupies, the age spread of the guests it draws and how far the rooms sit from the entertainment, not by the number of restaurants listed. Cap Cana rather than the middle of the strip when quiet matters more than the buffet count. One day on a private catamaran instead of the party boat, one round at Punta Espada if there is a golfer, and one afternoon inland so the children see a Dominican town. Five nights is usually right. Seven starts to feel like the same day.

Why Plan With Us

What We Add to Dominican Republic Planning

Here the online research is actively misleading, because the photographs are accurate and the descriptions are not.

⬡
Which Airport, and What It Costs You
Four airports are worth considering and they are nowhere near one another. Punta Cana has the schedule depth, which is why most itineraries default to it and why so many trips begin with a long transfer somewhere else. La Romana sits minutes from the Casa de Campo gate but runs a thin route map that varies by season. Santo Domingo is right for the capital and reasonable for the peninsula. El Catey is closest to Samaná and least dependable. The Instituto Dominicano de Aviación Civil publishes the current list; the decision is a trade between routing and daylight, and we make it first.
⬡
Reading All-Inclusives Honestly
"All-inclusive" is a billing model, not a rating, and it covers properties that photograph identically. Two resorts on the same beach can differ in the age of the guests they draw, the noise carried from the entertainment area after nine, whether the good restaurants are included or sold as an upgrade tier, and whether the sand in front is seaweed-prone in a given month. None of that appears in a listing. It appears in client reports and direct supplier contact — the same reading we apply across every all-inclusive resort we plan in the region.
⬡
Whale Season on the Right Dates
Humpback season in Samaná Bay is short, and the shoulders of it are not the same trip. Arrive in December or late April and the bay is beautiful and empty of whales. The middle of the window is when numbers are highest and boats go out most days. Access is regulated: operators are permitted, boat numbers capped and time near a group limited, which is why the trip is worth taking and why the good operators fill early. We book two separate mornings, because one booking against a windy day is how people go home having seen the bay and not the whales.
⬡
Golf Sequencing, Not Just Tee Times
The two strongest golf clusters sit at opposite ends of the country, and the itineraries that fail are the ones that try to play both from one base. Casa de Campo carries the deepest set of courses and the shortest walk from villa to first tee; Cap Cana and the Punta Cana resorts carry the eastern group. Driving between them for a single round burns most of a day each way. Pick the base by the golf that matters most, book the marquee round early in the stay so weather gets a second chance at it, and put a rest day between the two hardest walks.
When to Go

The Dominican Republic by Season

Dry Season
December – April
The window, and the reason the Dominican calendar is less flexible than the year-round marketing suggests. Drier air, steadier trade winds, the clearest water of the year and the lowest chance of a washed-out afternoon. Humpbacks are in Samaná Bay across the middle of it. This is also peak demand: the villas at Casa de Campo, the small hotels on the peninsula and the permitted whale operators commit months out, and Christmas, New Year and Easter are hardest of all to move. If school holidays fix your dates, book earlier than feels necessary.
Best Overall Window
Warm Shoulder
May – July
Hotter, wetter and considerably quieter, with afternoon rain that usually passes rather than settles. The Atlantic hurricane season opens on June 1, but the risk in these first weeks is low against what follows, which makes late May and June the most underrated stretch on the Dominican calendar. Cabarete's wind is at its most consistent now, so this is the strongest window for a kiteboarding trip and a weak one for whales. Travel insurance stops being optional from June onward.
Hurricane Peak
August – November
The National Hurricane Center puts the climatological peak of Atlantic activity in mid-September, with the busiest stretch running mid-August into late October. Rates fall for a reason. A trip in this window is defensible with flexible bookings, real insurance and a tolerance for changing plans at short notice, and indefensible if the dates cannot move. Late November recovers quickly and is one of the quieter good weeks of the year, just ahead of the December rush.

Season windows and whale dates verified August 2026. Operator permits, sailing dates and airline schedules change; confirm before booking. Sources: NOAA National Hurricane Center, Ministerio de Medio Ambiente.

What It Costs

What the Dominican Republic Actually Costs

Sold per all-inclusive room-night or per villa week
A Punta Cana all-inclusive is quoted per person with food, drink and tax already inside it, while a Casa de Campo villa is quoted for the whole house before an 18% ITBIS and the 10% legal service charge land on top — those are two products on two bases, not two points on one band.
What actually sets the number
  • Whether the rate is gross or net of 18% ITBIS and the 10% service charge
  • All-inclusive room-nights against a villa let by the house for the same party
  • The mid-January to late March humpback window, when peninsula hotels commit early

Tell me the dates and the party and you get a real quote, not a range. Source: Dominican ITBIS rate (DGII).

Common Questions

Dominican Republic — FAQ

The questions that come up most on the phone — which airport, whether Punta Cana is the right call, when the whales are in Samaná Bay, and how much one trip can honestly cover.

December through April, and the whole country agrees on it. That stretch is drier, the water clearest and the odds of losing an afternoon to rain lowest. It is also peak demand, so villas, small hotels and whale operators commit months ahead. The National Hurricane Center puts the Atlantic season from June 1 to November 30, with the climatological peak in mid-September, which makes August through October the window to avoid unless bookings are flexible. Late May, June and late November are the quiet edges: warmer, wetter, emptier, and clear of the busiest storm weeks.

La Romana if you are going to Casa de Campo and a workable flight exists; Punta Cana otherwise. The estate sits minutes from the La Romana terminal, which buys back most of an afternoon at each end. The catch is schedule depth: La Romana's route map is thin, and what flies in January may not fly in September. Punta Cana carries the volume and the choice, at the cost of a long transfer to anywhere outside the eastern corridor. Santo Domingo suits the capital and works for the peninsula; El Catey is closest to Samaná and least dependable. The airport list comes from the Instituto Dominicano de Aviación Civil; confirm routings before booking.

Roughly mid-January to late March, with February the most reliable weeks. North Atlantic humpbacks migrate from cold northern feeding waters to the warm Caribbean each winter to breed and calve, the behaviour described by NOAA Fisheries, and Samaná Bay is one of the most dependable places on earth to watch it from a small boat. Access is regulated by the Ministerio de Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales: operators are permitted, boat numbers around a group capped and time on the water limited. Book two separate mornings; weather cancels boats, and a single outing gives the trip one chance. Season dates shift year to year; confirm before booking.

Punta Cana is worth it for exactly one kind of trip, and it does that trip better than almost anywhere. That trip is a beach week with young children where food, drink and entertainment are handled and nobody makes a decision after breakfast — the case we make for family travel built around the children rather than the itinerary. What Punta Cana is not is a way to see the Dominican Republic: there is no town to walk into, and the country is at Casa de Campo, on the Samaná peninsula and in Santo Domingo. Choose deliberately and either trip works. Choose by accident and you booked the wrong country.

Casa de Campo, and it is not close. Teeth of the Dog is the Pete Dye design the estate was built around, and its shoreline holes are why it has held its reputation for more than fifty years; Dye Fore is the more dramatic course and the weaker one. Tee-time policy comes from Casa de Campo directly. In the east, Punta Espada at Cap Cana is the strongest card outside La Romana, and Corales at Puntacana Resort hosts a PGA Tour event, the clearest signal of conditioning there. The mistake is basing in one cluster and driving to the other for a single round: most of a day each way.

No, most US, Canadian, UK and EU visitors do not need a visa for a tourist stay. What is required is an electronic entry and exit form, completed online before each flight, and the QR code is asked for at check-in as well as on arrival. The official form lives at the Dirección General de Migración e-Ticket portal and it is free — anything charging you for it is not the government. Passport validity, permitted length of stay and entry rules differ by nationality and change; US travellers should read the State Department country page. Verify before booking flights, not in the departure hall.

Six to eight nights for a single base, and ten to twelve if you want two. The island is larger than the map suggests, and the pairs that work sit genuinely near each other: Santo Domingo with Casa de Campo, or Santo Domingo with the Samaná peninsula. Punta Cana with Samaná is the pairing people ask for most and the one that costs the most driving, because the road runs the long way around the bay — the better part of two days in a vehicle out of seven nights. Short trip: one base, day trips out. At ten nights or more, two bases and one transfer holds up.

An all-inclusive for a first trip with young children; a villa with staff for anything longer than a week or a group over six. The all-inclusive removes decisions, which is its whole value. Its cost is sameness, and a ceiling on how much of the country reaches you. A staffed villa at Casa de Campo or a small owner-run hotel on the peninsula gives you a cook, your own hours and a town to walk into, and asks for more decisions in return. Beyond about eight nights, most people who have done both prefer the second; below five nights with small children, most prefer the first.
